name: NIST AI RMF Characteristics of Trustworthy AI
publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
description: The seven characteristics of trustworthy AI in the AI RMF. They are not risks themselves; a shortfall in any of them is a source of AI risk, so they are commonly used as risk dimensions.

categories.name: Valid and Reliable
categories.description: Accuracy, reliability and robustness: the system fulfils its intended requirements and performs as required over time.

categories.name: Safe
categories.description: The system does not, under defined conditions, lead to a state in which human life, health, property or the environment is endangered.

categories.name: Secure and Resilient
categories.description: The system can withstand unexpected adverse events and maintain confidentiality, integrity and availability against attacks.

categories.name: Accountable and Transparent
categories.description: Information about the system and its outputs is available to those interacting with it; accountability presupposes transparency.

categories.name: Explainable and Interpretable
categories.description: The mechanisms underlying the system's operation (explainability) and the meaning of its outputs (interpretability) can be understood.

categories.name: Privacy-Enhanced
categories.description: Norms and practices that safeguard human autonomy, identity and dignity, such as limiting observation and protecting personal data.

categories.name: Fair – with Harmful Bias Managed
categories.description: Concerns for equality and equity, addressing harmful bias and discrimination (systemic, computational/statistical and human-cognitive bias).

record_provenance.notes: Hand-authored by the compiler from the publication. Names follow AI RMF 1.0 Section 3; descriptions are short paraphrases.
